root_cause.text: In `io_uring/zcrx`, the post-open error path in `io_register_zcrx_ifq()` freed the `io_zcrx_ifq`/zcrx context directly instead of unregistering it through the normal reference-counted teardown, which could destroy the context while associated page pools were still active.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the failure path from `io_zcrx_ifq_free(ifq);` to `zcrx_unregister(ifq);` and the commit message explicitly says “Closing a queue doesn't guarantee that all associated page pools are terminated right away, let the refcounting do the work instead of releasing the zcrx ctx directly”; it also removes the early `if (ifq->if_rxq == -1) return;` and only calls `net_mp_close_rxq()` when `if_rxq != -1`, showing the bug was premature teardown during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect early exit so queue cleanup always runs in io_close_queue().
intent_record.what: The early return that exited io_close_queue() when ifq->if_rxq was -1 was removed, so the function now always enters the scoped mutex-protected block and proceeds with the cleanup logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, io_close_queue() will no longer skip teardown for queues whose if_rxq field is -1, which means the associated network device cleanup and related state handling will run unconditionally instead of being bypassed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip closing the RX queue when it is already invalid by checking for -1 before calling net_mp_close_rxq().
intent_record.what: In io_close_queue(), the call to net_mp_close_rxq(netdev, ifq->if_rxq, &p) was wrapped in a conditional so it only executes when ifq->if_rxq != -1; the existing netdev_put() call and the assignment ifq->if_rxq = -1 remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now avoids attempting to close an invalid or already-cleared RX queue index represented by -1. This prevents an unnecessary or potentially unsafe close operation while still releasing the netdev reference and marking the queue as closed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error-path cleanup in io_register_zcrx_ifq() by routing teardown through zcrx_unregister() and removing redundant netdev reference release.
intent_record.what: In the error path of io_register_zcrx_ifq(), the direct call to netdev_put(ifq->netdev, &ifq->netdev_tracker) was removed from the netdev_put_unlock label, and the cleanup call io_zcrx_ifq_free(ifq) was replaced with zcrx_unregister(ifq) at the ifq_free label.
intent_record.how: On failure, cleanup now delegates to zcrx_unregister(ifq) instead of freeing the ifqueue structure directly, which likely centralizes teardown and ensures associated unregister/release steps happen in the correct order. Removing the explicit netdev_put from this path suggests that reference release is now handled inside the new unregister helper, preventing double-release or inconsistent cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The change addresses cleanup flow in io_uring/zcrx by removing an early exit so queue teardown always runs. That is directly related to the root cause, which was improper direct freeing instead of going through the normal teardown/unregister path.

The change only avoids calling net_mp_close_rxq() on an already invalid RX queue. It does not address the zcrx post-open error path, reference-counted teardown, or the premature freeing of io_zcrx_ifq/context while page pools remain active.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the error-path cleanup in io_register_zcrx_ifq() to use the normal zcrx_unregister() teardown instead of directly freeing the zcrx context, preventing premature destruction while related page pools may still be active.

candidates.rationale: This direct free on the error path bypasses the normal unregister/teardown flow, matching the root cause where the zcrx context could be destroyed while related page pools or other references were still active.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path cleanup directly frees the io_zcrx_ifq/zcrx context instead of going through the normal reference-counted unregister path, which could destroy the context while page pools or other references were still active.

    using a new registration opcode IORING_REGISTER_ZCRX_IFQ.
